candidates.title: Optimal-transport flow matching for stochastic model ipdating
candidates.abstract: Deep generative models have attracted considerable attention as inference engines for stochastic model updating. Among these deep generative models, conditional flow matching offers a particularly efficient formulation, in which a continuous transport map from a latent distribution to the posterior is learned by regression against optimal-transport probability paths, avoiding both the invertibility constraints of normalising flows and the iterative denoising of diffusion models. However, its performance in engineering model updating has not been examined against an established baseline such as the Bayesian updating framework under controlled conditions. In this work, conditional flow matching is therefore assessed against the Bayesian model updating approach with transitional Markov chain Monte Carlo, in which the Bhattacharyya distance provides the approximate likelihood for the Bayesian approach. The two methods are assessed with respect to posterior fidelity, evaluated by statistical distances against the known ground truth and computational expenditure in model evaluations, with the offline training budget reported separately from the inference cost of each subsequent conditioning. A 3-DOF spring–mass system with uncertain stiffness parameters serves as the benchmark. Since the calibrated posterior constitutes the input description upon which subsequent reliability assessment depends, the accuracy and the marginal cost of the updating step both bear directly on reliability computations. In addition, the amortised nature of the learned transport map is discussed in this work, as it permits the posterior to be re-evaluated under new observations at negligible cost, which is a property of practical relevance to reliability assessment under sequentially acquired monitoring data.

candidates.title: Evaluating Machine Learning Affinity Prediction Methods on Novel Lead Optimization Data: A 15‐PGDH Case Study
candidates.abstract: Recent machine learning (ML) methods for protein–ligand affinity prediction, such as Boltz‐2 and AEV‐PLIG, have been reported to approach free energy perturbation (FEP) accuracy on well‐known benchmarks. Even short of that accuracy, ML‐based potency models that fall between FEP and common docking scoring functions in accuracy and speed offer clear potential value. Here, we report a case study using recently disclosed data from four related ligand series targeting 15‐hydroxyprostaglandin dehydrogenase (15‐PGDH). We evaluate each ML method's predictive accuracy with a focus on when it could be used to influence synthetic priorities. AEV‐PLIG performed poorly across most series, and adding literature 15‐PGDH inhibitors to its training did not improve performance. Boltz‐2 performed well on series most similar to published inhibitors in its training, achieving accurate cofolding (median ligand RMSD ≤0.81 Å) and rank order. However, for a series exploring a new region of the binding pocket, Boltz‐2 sometimes generated less accurate poses and predicted all ligands in the series to be less potent than a published exemplar, despite experimental potency gains of up to 500x. These results highlight both the promise in well‐characterized chemical space and limitations in the novel regions where computational guidance is most needed.

candidates.title: qcGEM: A Graph-Based Molecular Representation With Quantum Chemistry Awareness.
candidates.abstract: The advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has reshaped drug discovery. AI-based models typically rely on molecular representations for prediction. However, the absence of physically grounded information in mainstream molecular representations not only limits the model performance in practical applications but also hinders mechanistic understanding and exploitation by humans. To overcome this issue, we introduce qcGEM, a quantum-chemistry-aware graph-based embedding of molecules that incorporates physical priors into molecular representation learning. Through a specially designed model architecture to adequately process quantum chemistry information, qcGEM provides a compact, physics-informed molecular representation that supports a diverse range of downstream applications. Particularly, qcGEM demonstrates state-of-the-art performance across a broad range of molecule-related benchmarks, as evidenced by comprehensive evaluations on 83 tasks including molecular property prediction, activity cliff detection, protein-ligand interaction modeling, and opioid drug regression, and simultaneously offers strong interpretability at multiple representation levels. We additionally propose a simplified variant, qcGEM-Hybrid, with substantially accelerated embedding generation and robust performance. Overall, our method provides an advanced molecular representation that will benefit molecule-related modeling and prediction, supporting further progress in AI-aided drug discovery.

candidates.title: Exploring the Upper Boundaries of Distance-Based Protein-Ligand Binding Affinity Prediction: Accuracy Improvements via Linear Regression and Artificial Neural Networks
candidates.abstract: The traditional scoring functions for protein-ligand binding affinity prediction usually adopt fixed mathematical formulas to characterize atomic interaction energies, where electrostatic interactions are described by the a/r function and van der Waals interactions by the b/r^6 -c/r^12 function. These fixed power exponents of distance-based variables severely limit the predictive flexibility and generalization of conventional scoring models. To address this limitation, this study proposes an improved prediction strategy with unrestricted power exponents for distance-dependent atomic interaction variables. To explore the upper boundaries of the predictive powers, the optimized distance-based descriptors were integrated with linear regression and artificial neural network algorithms to construct novel models for protein-ligand binding affinity and binding energy prediction. All linear, artificial neural network, and hybrid models in this work were trained and validated on the latest high-quality dataset from PDBbind (version 2024). Quantitative evaluation based on the Pearson's correlation coefficient (R) demonstrated that the optimized linear models achieved a moderate predictive performance with R values ranging from 0.700 to 0.800 on the high-quality affinity dataset, while the artificial neural network-based hybrid models yielded substantially improved accuracy, with R values between 0.800 and 0.900. Comparative analysis verified that the optimal models established in this study outperform previously-reported state-of-the-art linear and machine learning-based scoring functions. Specially, this work indicates that the scoring functions with explicit mathematical expressions can achieve a high accuracy close to the experimental error for affinity prediction in a dataset composed of several thousand protein-ligand complexes. The overall results indicate that rationally-optimized power exponents for distance-based variables can effectively enhance the predictive accuracy of protein-ligand binding affinity prediction, providing a reliable and efficient tool for computational drug discovery.

candidates.title: DNA-Encoded Library-Guided Discovery of a First-in-Class Molecular Glue of the NOS1AP-SCRIB Complex in Alzheimer's Disease Patient-Derived Neurons
candidates.abstract: NOS1AP is an adaptor for neuronal nitric oxide synthase that engages several partner proteins and is implicated in Alzheimer's disease. Efforts to drug NOS1AP have sought to disrupt these; we instead report pharmacological stabilization of one interaction. Affinity selection of a 1.4-billion-member DNA-encoded library identified a benzimidazole-5-carboxamide chemotype, optimized by fragment-directed SAR to NOSTRA with submicromolar NOS1AP binding affinity. Of six interactions, NOSTRA enhanced only SCRIB binding, with a cooperativity factor of 30, predominantly through a 14-fold slowing of dissociation; native mass spectrometry resolved a NOS1AP:NOSTRA:SCRIB ternary complex. In healthy human iPSC-derived cortical neurons, NOSTRA engaged the endogenous complex and activated Rac1 without cytotoxicity; in Alzheimer's patient-derived neurons, it lowered the A{beta}42/A{beta}40 ratio and p-tau217, reduced neurofilament light and improved network activity. With an in vitro ADME profile consistent with CNS exposure, NOSTRA is the first molecular glue for a NOS1AP complex, establishing interaction stabilization as a viable NOS1AP pharmacology.

candidates.title: A Hybrid Multi-Objective Hyperparameter Optimization with an Efficiency Score for Brain Tumor Classification
candidates.abstract: This repository contains the complete reproducibility package for the paper *"A Hybrid Multi-Objective Hyperparameter Optimization with an Efficiency Score for Brain Tumor Classification"*. The proposed framework combines three components: 1. *Hyperband** — fast low-budget screening of hyperparameters (Phase 1) 2. *Bayesian Optimization** — Gaussian-process refinement under Pareto constraints on accuracy and latency (Phase 2) 3. Efficiency-δ Metric** — a novel compound score jointly rewarding accuracy, throughput, and model compactness: The model is evaluated on the **Brain Tumor MRI Dataset** and demonstrates significant improvement over the baseline EfficientNet-B3.

candidates.title: PATHNet: A Thermodynamic Path-Integral-Inspired Neural Network for Protein-Ligand Interaction Prediction
candidates.abstract: Protein-ligand scoring functions must capture strongly nonlinear, target-dependent binding physics while remaining generalizable beyond their training data, a balance that purely analytic and purely data-driven models each struggle to achieve on their own. We present PATHNet, a physics-informed framework that learns this unknown functional relationship from molecular-mechanics descriptors using a non-monotonic piecewise-linear mapper with a bounded neural-network correction, trained through a variational, least-action-inspired objective and regulated by a renormalization-group-inspired spectral constraint, with model selection performed through multi-start basin optimization. Across seven DUD-E targets, PATHNet achieved the highest mean active inactive/decoy classification accuracy among the methods tested, outperforming three literature baselines representing distinct architectural families. These results support a physics-grounded, variationally constrained approach to neural-network scoring as a practical route toward more interpretable and transferable protein-ligand interaction models.

candidates.title: A Hybrid Computational Intelligence Framework for Automatic Calibration of Catchment Scale Hydrodynamic Flood Models
candidates.abstract: Abstract This study presents a novel automated framework for the calibration and validation of rain-on-grid (RoG) hydrodynamic models at the catchment scale, with specific application to the TUFLOW HPC platform. The proposed approach establishes an integrated and automated workflow that links rainfall input directly to flood response, enabling efficient calibration of key hydraulic parameters, including Manning’s roughness, initial loss, and continuous loss. The framework combines ensemble-based parameter sampling, automated model execution, data-driven surrogate modelling, and evolutionary optimization algorithms (EAs) to systematically explore parameter combinations within the defined calibration ranges. Three modelling techniques—Random Forest (RF), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), and Gradient Boosting (GB)—are employed to approximate model responses from an ensemble of hydrodynamic model simulations, thereby accelerating the calibration process and reducing computational costs. Furthermore, three EAs, consisting of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Invasive Weed Optimization (IWO), and Differential Evolution (DE), are applied. The optimization objective is defined as minimizing the discrepancy between simulated and reference inundation extents, quantified through total inundated area derived from benchmark inundation datasets. The entire process is implemented in a MATLAB-based script that automatically controls TUFLOW simulations, iteratively adjusts parameters, and evaluates model performance without manual intervention. The framework is tested in a small catchment case study under multiple design rainfall events (50-, 100-, and 500-year return periods). Results demonstrate close agreement between the simulated and reference inundation areas, with differences of less than 1% across all scenarios. These findings indicate satisfactory predictive performance within the studied calibration range. The key novelty of this study lies in the integration of surrogate-assisted optimization within a fully automated calibration environment tailored for RoG models. Furthermore, the developed MATLAB code is made publicly available via GitHub, promoting transparency, reproducibility, and potential broader application in hydrodynamic flood modelling.

candidates.title: A multi‑modal recognition method for building structural materials integrating structured text description and adaptive decision weighting
candidates.abstract: Accurate identification of building structural materials is a critical step in structural safety assessment and damage detection. Traditional image‑based classification methods are limited by factors such as illumination, occlusion, and surface treatment, making it difficult to effectively distinguish different materials using visual features alone. To address this problem, an intelligent recognition method for building structural materials based on multi‑modal data fusion is proposed. First, a prompting method based on a multi‑modal large language model is designed to generate structured text descriptions tailored to material classification tasks, covering discriminative information such as surface characteristics, geometric details, signs of degradation, and material inference. Second, a multi‑modal neural network named MRNet is proposed. It introduces a lightweight text feature transformer that reshapes the global vector from the Contrastive Language‑Image Pre‑training (CLIP) text encoder into a sequence and adds positional encoding. A lightweight text-feature encoder further refines the CLIP global text embedding through nonlinear transformation and channel mixing, alleviating the information compression caused by the original CLIP global pooling. The model adopts a decision‑level learnable weighted fusion strategy, where the decision results from the image and text modalities are fused through a learnable linear layer, enabling efficient cross‑modal integration without complex feature alignment. Furthermore, Bayesian optimization is introduced to automatically tune key hyperparameters such as learning rate, batch size, and weight decay coefficient. Experimental results on the PEER dataset show that MRNet achieves 96.00% in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score, significantly outperforming mainstream image classification models such as AlexNet, MobileNet‑v3, ResNet, and VGG. The proposed method provides a high‑accuracy, high‑efficiency multi‑modal solution for building structural material identification.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence Framework for Drug-Target Affinity Prediction Using Deep Neural Networks and Integrated Molecular and Protein Feature Engineering
candidates.abstract: Objective: To develop an artificial intelligence framework that integrates deep neural networks with molecular and protein feature engineering to accurately predict drug-target affinity, thereby supporting efficient computational drug discovery and therapeutic candidate identification.The proposed study employed a publicly available drug-target affinity dataset consisting of molecular SMILES representations, protein amino acid sequences, and experimentally determined affinity values, partitioned into training, validation, and testing subsets for model development.Material and Methods: A publicly available drug-target affinity dataset containing training, validation, and testing subsets was employed, in which molecular SMILES representations and protein sequences were converted into integrated numerical descriptors through feature engineering and standardized before model training.Subsequently, a Deep Neural Network (DNN) was developed to capture the complex relationships between the engineered molecular and protein features for accurate drug-target affinity prediction.Extracting representative features from molecular SMILES representations and protein sequences remains a major challenge in accurately predicting drug-target affinity.Capturing the complex nonlinear relationships between drug molecules and target proteins is further complicated by the high dimensionality and intricate nature of biological data.Results: To mitigate these challenges, a Deep Neural Network integrated with molecular and protein feature engineering was employed to candidates.title: Longitudinal associations between task-control network functioning, cognition, and the environment in early adolescence
candidates.abstract: Neural maturation in the "task-control" frontoparietal and dorsal attention networks is thought to support the development of adolescents' cognitive and adaptive functioning. Further, theory suggests that family and neighborhood contexts shape brain network development. Yet, few longitudinal studies have examined the co-development of brain network mechanisms with cognitive and adaptive functioning or with environmental factors that could shape the maturation of these mechanisms. The present study addressed these gaps. We used longitudinal data spanning late childhood (Mage=10 years) to early adolescence (Mage=12) from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study (n=4862). Stable and construct-valid neural signatures of task-control network functioning were estimated using longitudinal bifactor modeling of neural responses to cognitive demand during the n-back task. Multivariate latent change-score models were used to examine co-development of this signature with cognitive efficiency (drift rate from the diffusion model), teacher-reported attention problems, family conflict, and neighborhood safety. Models accounted for baseline family income. Robust reciprocal relations between task-control activation and cognitive efficiency were identified and the latent change scores for efficiency and task-control activation were positively correlated. Similar reciprocal associations were observed between cognitive efficiency and attention problems. Baseline family income predicted the rate of change in task-control network functioning. This study demonstrates that task-control network functioning co-develops with cognition, which in turn supports attentional functioning development across early adolescence. Further, findings highlight the utility of this neural signature of task-control network functioning for understanding the neural basis of cognitive development and the mechanisms through which environmental experiences shape brain and behavior.

candidates.title: Channelrhodopsin ion selectivity determines mechanisms and efficacy of optogenetic defibrillation in human atria and ventricles
candidates.abstract: Abstract Cardiac re‐entrant arrhythmias are a major cause of sudden cardiac death. Optogenetic defibrillation has emerged as a promising anti‐arrhythmic strategy based on photoactivation of channelrhodopsins, yet the efficacy and potential adverse consequences of activating different classes of light‐gated ion channels have not been systematically evaluated. Previous studies assessed either cation (e.g. ChR2) or anion (e.g. GtACR1) non‐selective channels, both of which depolarize resting cardiomyocytes. Recently identified light‐gated K + channels (e.g. WiChR) suppress cardiomyocyte activity while maintaining the membrane potential near its resting state, but their defibrillation potential remains unexplored. We used computational simulations to compare ChR2, GtACR1 and WiChR. Single‐cell simulations showed that ChR2 and GtACR1 markedly increased diastolic intracellular Ca 2+ (by 42.6% and 52.6%, respectively), whereas WiChR induced only minimal changes (by 4.0%), suggesting lower pro‐arrhythmogenic risk. WiChR, however, slightly increased intracellular Na + (by 15.1% vs . 0.1% and 3.4% for ChR2 and GtACR1), consistent with the residual Na + permeability of currently available K + ‐conducting channelrhodopsins. Simulations in human ventricles and atria showed that GtACR1 most effectively terminated re‐entrant arrhythmias at low light intensities, whereas WiChR achieved comparable efficacy at ≥5 mW/mm 2 . Complementary tissue‐scale simulations revealed that defibrillation occurs through depolarization within the excitable gap followed by fast Na + channel inactivation (ChR2 and partly GtACR1), or through reduced membrane resistance at sufficiently high light intensities (large‐conductance channels GtACR1 and WiChR). Overall, we demonstrate that channelrhodopsin ion selectivity is a key determinant of both optogenetic defibrillation efficacy and its underlying mechanisms. image Translational perspective Re‐entrant arrhythmias are a leading cause of sudden cardiac death. Standard therapies, including the activation of implantable cardioverter‐defibrillators, carry burdens such as pain and myocardial injury. Optogenetic defibrillation has been suggested as a potentially gentler alternative, replacing high‐voltage electrical shocks by photoactivation of light‐gated ion channels expressed in cardiac cells. Determining which light‐gated ion channel optimally balances efficacy and adverse effects on cardiac electrophysiology is critical for clinical translation. We addressed this question using computational simulations and validation experiments in zebrafish hearts. We identify ion selectivity as a key determinant of both the success rate for arrhythmia termination and the underlying mechanisms: non‐selective cation‐ and anion‐conducting channels terminate re‐entry efficiently while promoting intracellular Ca 2+ accumulation, a plausible substrate for pro‐arrhythmic side effects that could undermine therapeutic safety. K + ‐conducting channels largely avoid this pro‐arrhythmic risk by holding cardiomyocytes near their resting potential, albeit at the cost of requiring transmural illumination, while also causing mild Na + accumulation attributable to residual Na + permeability. Together, these trade‐offs define clear clinical implications: K + ‐conducting channels may provide the safest option for optogenetic defibrillation, particularly once variants with further enhanced K + selectivity and red‐shifted activation spectra for improved operation within blood‐perfused myocardium become available. Key points We use computational simulations to compare cation non‐selective (ChR2), anion non‐selective (GtACR1) and K + ‐selective (WiChR) channelrhodopsins for optogenetic termination of re‐entrant arrhythmia. Single‐cardiomyocyte simulations suggest that ChR2 and GtACR1 activation can cause progressive accumulation of intracellular Ca 2+ , which is minimized when using WiChR. Intracellular microelectrode recordings from hearts of transgenic adult zebrafish validate the simulated voltage dynamics seen with ChR2, GtACR1 or WiChR activation. Simulations of human left ventricles and atria indicate that GtACR1 is most effective in terminating re‐entrant arrhythmia at low light intensities, whereas WiChR becomes similarly effective at higher intensities. Tissue‐scale simulations indicate distinct defibrillation mechanisms: excitable gap extinction by de novo action potential initiation followed by inactivation of fast Na + channels for depolarizing channelrhodopsins (ChR2, GtACR1), and reduction in membrane resistance for the large‐conductance channels (GtACR1, WiChR), effectively clamping the membrane potential at each channel's reversal potential at high light levels.

candidates.title: A simple platform for in situ DNA-PAINT optimization enables improved multiplexed super-resolution imaging in Gram-negative bacteria
candidates.abstract: DNA-PAINT enables super-resolution imaging with high multiplexing capacity, yet it is rarely used in nanoscale bacteriology. A likely reason is the lack of straightforward protocols and of systematic characterization of imager-docking strand pairs inside intact bacterial cells, whose envelope and dense cytoplasm differ markedly from both the DNA origami in vitro systems used to develop them, and eukaryotic cells. In this work, we establish a screening platform based on RNA-FISH, in which we extend the 16S rRNA-directed EUB338 probe with docking sequences of choice. This allows imager-docking pairs to be benchmarked directly inside Escherichia coli cells and characterized for parameters such as specificity, binding kinetics, and localization precision. We screened 12 different DNA-PAINT sequences and used an optimized set to perform four-target 3D Exchange-PAINT in single E. coli cells. We further applied our strategy to image three effector mRNAs in the Gram-negative pathogen Yersinia enterocolitica and quantified RNA clusters and their 3D distribution. Our work provides a framework and practical guidelines for high-quality 3D DNA-PAINT imaging in Gram-negative bacteria and should facilitate its broader adoption in nanoscale bacteriology.

candidates.title: Sequence-based artificial intelligence-guided inhibitory peptides to counteract AAV neutralizing antibodies in gene therapy.
candidates.abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors have demonstrated strong clinical efficacy across multiple monogenic disorders, yet neutralizing antibodies (NAbs) remain major barriers to vector redosing and durable transduction. To address this limitation, we developed a sequence-based artificial intelligence framework integrating Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) and Evolutionary Scale Modeling with Low-Rank Adaptation (ESM-LoRA) to identify human-tolerant, virus-specific motifs across human and viral proteins using sliding-window analyses and multi-layer fine-tuning. Using capsid-derived segments from AAV2 and AAV843, we prioritized surface-accessible, virus-polarized peptides as candidate decoys and evaluated their ability to block AAV-targeted antibodies. The models achieved high accuracy in distinguishing human versus viral fragments, and selected peptides bound AAV-specific antibodies with nanomolar affinity, competitively restored capsid binding, and recovered >60% of baseline transduction in the presence of NAbs. In mouse models with pre-existing or redosing-induced antibodies, coadministration of decoy peptides and an IgG-degrading enzyme reduced high-titer NAbs to approximately 1:4 and restored hepatic transgene expression without detectable inflammatory or peptide-specific immune responses. A contrastive variational autoencoder (VAE) further generated non-natural peptides with broader epitope coverage. These results support sequence-driven AI design of short, low-immunogenicity decoy peptides as a translational strategy to mitigate NAb interference and enhance the feasibility of AAV redosing.

candidates.title: Fast Solution Methods for the Classical 0–1 Knapsack Problem
candidates.abstract: The classical 0--1 knapsack problem is among the simplest integer programs to state and among the most instructive problems for understanding why algorithm selection must follow instance structure. An input contains items with positive integer weights and profits, and the task is to choose a maximum-profit subset whose total weight does not exceed a capacity. The problem is weakly NP-hard, yet many large instances are solved quickly because exact algorithms exploit moderate numeric parameters, strong linear relaxations, dominance relations, or a small set of uncertain variables near the fractional break item. This review develops a theory-guided account of the principal fast solution methods for the classical problem. It proves the correctness and complexity of weight-indexed and profit-indexed dynamic programming, explains sparse Pareto-frontier implementations and reconstruction, derives the fractional-knapsack upper bound used by branch-and-bound methods, and establishes the correctness of meet-in-the-middle search. It then presents the core concept that underlies influential practical solvers and gives a detailed proof of the standard profit-scaling fully polynomial-time approximation scheme. Modern advances based on structured min-plus convolution are placed within this classical landscape rather than treated as isolated results. The central conclusion is that there is no universally fastest knapsack algorithm. Small item counts favor meet-in-the-middle search, moderate capacities or total profits favor dynamic programming, favorable density structure favors core-based exact methods, and very large numeric coefficients favor approximation. A final decision framework translates these theoretical distinctions into an implementable solver-selection policy while identifying open questions concerning adaptivity, certified switching among methods, memory efficiency, and realistic hard-instance generation.

candidates.title: Accelerating Molecular Dynamics with Hydrogen Mass Repartitioning to Prioritize Immunogenic Neoantigens for Cancer Vaccines through Peptide HLA Binding Free Energy Calculations
candidates.abstract: Personalized neoantigen based vaccines have progressed from concept to clinical evidence for some of the most aggressive human tumors, yet a key challenge remains: determining which candidates should be prioritized for vaccine inclusion. Public neoantigens, shared across tumor subtypes and patient populations, offer potential as off the shelf candidates for broad spectrum immunotherapy. Candidate selection relies on in silico pipelines that estimate binding; however, binding affinity alone is an imperfect marker of immunogenicity. Molecular dynamics (MD) combined with endpoint free energy methods estimates binding free energy directly from simulated trajectories, and hydrogen mass repartitioning (HMR) mitigates the computational cost of hydrogen involving bond vibrations. This study assessed whether HMR accelerated MD can prioritize immunogenic neoantigens through peptide HLA binding free energy calculations and quantified the trade off between accuracy and computational cost. Ten immunogenic public neoantigens (seven paired with their wild type counterparts and three frameshift neoantigens analyzed as unpaired references) were modeled in complex with their HLA I alleles, built de novo using AlphaFold3 and propagated with a 4 fs HMR time step. Mean binding free energy was computed across ten replicas per complex, and each SNV pair was scored concordant with experimental data when the neoantigen formed a more favorable complex than its wild type. Free energies were recomputed at 100 to 500 ns to identify the shortest trajectory preserving reliable ranking. Free energy calculations reproduced experimental concordance for six of seven SNV pairs and were inconclusive for TP53 R8H. Frameshift neoantigens yielded comparable values. Most complexes retained both peptide termini anchored to the HLA groove throughout, and RMSD and RMSF metrics agreed with one another and with the free energy rankings. The PIK3CA E545K (E11K) pair showed the most distinctive signature: the peptides engaged the groove almost identically over P1 to P8, with the entire difference confined to the C terminal pocket, where loss of the wild type's anchor also disrupted its backbone anchor. This pair showed the largest free energy separation in the panel, and restricting analysis to bound frames confirmed a substantial electrostatic and van der Waals advantage favoring the neoantigen. These findings support HMR accelerated binding free energy MD as a practical refinement step for neoantigen prioritization and its application to assessing public neoantigens for cancer vaccine design.

candidates.title: INTELLIGENT TASK SCHEDULING IN CLOUD ROBOTICS
candidates.abstract: Cloud robotics is an emerging multidisciplinary research area in computer science, combining cloud computing an Internetbased model for sharing computing resources and services via virtualization technologies with robotics to extend the scarce onboard resources and capabilities of robots.Scheduling search is still an open issue: scheduling (plans, decisions) involved in the starting execution placement and distribution of the execution of computational tasks across the Cloudrobotic local, the (robot) edge and the Cloud layers).This systematic comparative review and analysis of over 42 journal articles (2020-2026) regarding intelligent task scheduling algorithms-including classical heuristics, meta-heuristics, reinforcement learning, and deep learning-is not intended to be an exhaustive survey of the complete literature.This review is further enriched by empirical analysis of a real-world dataset of 12,000 cloud-robotic scheduling problems (Oct 2025Oct 2026) of CC01 cloud-robotic benchmark, featuring 8 tables of comparison, algorithm pseudocodes, system architecture and empirical results analysis.HAF hybrid adaptive configuration is a mixture of NSGA-II, Deep Q-Network with all the seven benchmark models.It boasts mean latency of 11.6 ms, resource use of 91.2%, a task completion fraction of 95.3%, and energy saving of 34.1%.The analysis of dataset and edge computing reveals that it acts as the top scheduling layer (48.3%) just for local execution, having 7.3 times lower latency than a cloud with a restricted capacity.

candidates.title: Source-Decomposed Multimodal Graph Connectivity: A Temporal Mixture-Manifold Pipeline for Tracking Ischemic Injury and Treatment
candidates.abstract: To capture the complex, dynamic network reorganization following acute focal brain injuries that standard static or unimodal neuroimaging frameworks routinely miss, we present an open, reproducible computational multimodal pipeline that integrates resting state functional MRI and diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) into dynamic, source-decomposed graph networks. This framework preserves sub-voxel, multi-peak distributional dynamics over time by modeling regional blood-oxygen-level-dependent signals within sliding windows using a Gaussian mixture model, with model complexity dynamically optimized. The resulting pairwise similarities define time-varying edge weights across local, nonlocal, and DTI-supported structural sources, unifying them into a multimodal connectivity manifold that precisely quantifies node strength, topological turnover, and boundary modifications. Applied to a non-human primate model of photothrombotic ischemia, the methodology revealed severe post-injury disruptions, with 66 of 144 nodes (45.8%) fundamentally altering their connectivity across localized sources. Furthermore, coupling this architecture with an Ensemble Kalman Filter (EnKF) allowed for the continuous tracking of a tissue reversibility coordinate, yielding earlier detection of metabolic state collapse than uni-modal baselines and generating a forecast-divergence index as a rigorous early-warning signal. Extended across post-injury treatment boundaries to evaluate network recovery toward baseline, this interpretable, modality-aware framework establishes a standardized, shareable methodological foundation for tracking complex pathophysiological dynamics in neuroinformatics research.

candidates.title: Adaptive storage optimization for deep learning workloads in converged HPC-cloud environments: a reinforcement learning approach
candidates.abstract: Abstract Storage systems remain a significant bottleneck in large-scale deep learning training. Most evaluation studies rely on synthetic benchmarks that do not capture the I/O heterogeneity present in real training pipelines. Automated configuration methods often treat parameter selection as stateless, overlooking the temporal structure of recurring training phases. These challenges are addressed using a converged HPC-cloud platform that integrates Lustre with S3-compatible object storage. Three workloads with distinct I/O characteristics were evaluated: ResNet-50 on ImageNet-1K, 3D U-Net on the Medical Segmentation Decathlon, and Whisper Large on LibriSpeech. Time-to-convergence was used as the primary metric. We introduced a deep reinforcement learning framework that combines Proximal Policy Optimization and Soft Actor-Critic with a Transformer-based state encoder to predict workload phase transitions rather than merely respond to them. The learned policies reduced checkpoint write latency by up to 74.6% and improved GPU utilization across all three workloads. The approach generalizes across heterogeneous I/O profiles without per-workload reconfiguration. The results indicate that temporally aware storage control can improve the efficiency of distributed training pipelines in heterogeneous HPC-cloud environments.

candidates.title: LigRNA: High-accuracy prediction of RNA-ligand binding sites via dynamic chemical complementarity and language model encoding
candidates.abstract: RNA-binding small molecules represent a validated therapeutic modality, yet pinpointing their exact RNA binding sites remains critical for mechanistic understanding and drug optimization. Experimental methods, while precise, are costly and low-throughput, necessitating robust computational alternatives. Approaches based on static feature concatenation may overlook input-dependent relationships between RNA residues and ligand functional groups. Here we present LigRNA, a graph neural network framework that predicts RNA-ligand binding sites through joint cross-modal encoding of both molecules. LigRNA integrates structure-guided language model embeddings with physicochemical features-solvent-accessible surface area and secondary structure types, to construct comprehensive RNA representations. Ligands are encoded as attributed molecular graphs via graph attention networks, preserving atom-level chemical topology rather than compressing molecules into fixed fingerprints. A cross-attention mechanism then enables dynamic, ligand-dependent modulation of RNA nucleotide attention, capturing context-specific interaction patterns. Benchmarked on TE9 and TE18 datasets, LigRNA achieves F1 scores of 0.73 and 0.58, improving on GATRsite by 7.4% and 18.4%, respectively. Ablation studies identify the RNA residual encoder as the most consistent contributor across the two benchmarks. The source code is freely available at https://github.com/WillowWang0216/LigRNA.

candidates.title: The hive mind is a single reinforcement learning agent
candidates.abstract: Abstract Decision-making is an essential attribute of any intelligent agent or group. Natural systems are known to converge to effective strategies through at least two distinct mechanisms: collective decision-making via imitation of others, and trial-and-error by a single agent. This paper establishes an equivalence between these two paradigms. We show that the emergent distributed cognition (sometimes referred to as the hive mind ) arising from individuals following simple, local imitation-based rules is that of a single online reinforcement learning (RL) agent aggregating action-value samples from many parallel instances of a multi-armed bandit. More specifically, we show that, in the blindly imitative weighted voter model of honey bees’ waggle dance, the update rule through which this macro-agent learns is an RL algorithm that we coin Maynard-Cross Learning . Our analysis implies that a group of individuals following simple imitative strategies can be equivalent to a more complex learning entity, substantiating the idea that group-level intelligence may explain how seemingly irrational individual behaviors are selected in nature. Beyond biology, the framework offers new tools for analyzing economic and social systems where individuals imitate successful strategies, effectively participating in a collective learning process. Our findings may further inform the design of scalable RL-inspired collective systems in artificial domains.

candidates.title: Functional characterization of a MatE transporter in Methermicoccus shengliensis and evolutionary diversity of archaeal MatE transporters
candidates.abstract: Archaea, one of the three domains of life, exhibit remarkable physiological diversity and occupy a wide spectrum of ecological niches, ranging from extreme environments such as hypersaline lakes, hot springs, and acidic or alkaline habitats to moderate ecosystems including marine, freshwater, terrestrial, oilfield and host-associated environments. Among them, methanogenic archaea are obligate anaerobes that produce methane through distinct methanogenic pathways, traditionally utilizing simple substrates such as H2/CO2, acetate, methanol, and methylated compounds. The recent discovery that Methermicoccus shengliensis can metabolize methoxylated aromatic compounds (MACs) has expanded the known substrate spectrum of methanogens. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the transport of these structurally complex compounds into archaeal cells remain unknown. In this study, we investigated the substrate transport system of M. shengliensis ZC-1 cultivated with methanol and 2-methoxybenzoate. Transcriptomic analysis identified two highly expressed genes, matE and tlp, potentially involved in substrate uptake. Integrating bioinformatic analyses, protein-protein interaction, and structural modeling assays, we propose a transport model comprising three sequential steps: the transduction like protein Tlp first recognizes the 2-methoxybenzoate extracellularly, then interacts with the transmembrane MATE family transporter MatE, and finally MatE mediates the translocation of the substrate into the cell. Deletion of MatE markedly impairs cell growth and methane production under methoxylated aromatic conditions, underscoring its critical role in methoxydotrophic methanogenesis. To further elucidate the diversity and habitat adaptation of archaeal MatE transporters, we performed large-scale comparative genomic phylogenetic analyses, combined with structural classification and molecular docking. Our results reveal that MatE transporters are widely distributed but unevenly represented across archaeal lineages, exhibiting structural diversity that can be classified into four major classes. Class I MatE is the most conserved and phylogenetically prevalent, whereas Classes II, III, and IV are comparatively rare. Notably, compared with MatE-negative genomes, MatE-positive archaeal genomes are significantly enriched in host-associated and hypersaline environments, as well as in heterotrophic lineages. Furthermore, specific MatE transporters exhibit strong associations with particular habitats, and their copy numbers are positively correlated with genome size. This non-random distribution indicates that the presence of MatE transporters is closely linked to specific ecological niches and metabolic strategies. Overall, this work uncovers a previously uncharacterized transport mechanism for methoxylated aromatic compounds in methanogenic archaea and provides a comprehensive framework for understanding the diversity and habitat adaptation of the archaeal MATE transporter family. These findings advance our understanding of substrate acquisition strategies and methane metabolism in archaea, provide new insights into their ecological distribution, and elucidate their adaptation to extreme environments, highlighting their biological importance and deepening our understanding of life on Earth.

candidates.title: Global Research Trends in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Drug Delivery Technology: A Bibliometric and Science Mapping Analysis (2015–2026)
candidates.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) have emerged as transformative technologies in pharmaceutical research, significantly influencing the design, optimization, and personalization of drug delivery systems.AI-assisted approaches are increasingly applied to predict drug release kinetics, optimize formulation parameters, identify novel drug carriers, enhance therapeutic efficacy, and accelerate pharmaceutical product development.Despite the rapid growth of this interdisciplinary research area, a comprehensive understanding of its global scientific evolution, collaborative networks, and emerging research themes remains limited.The present study aims to systematically map the global research landscape of AI and ML applications in drug delivery technology through a bibliometric analysis of publications published between 2015 and 2026.Bibliographic records will be retrieved from the Scopus database using a predefined search strategy, screened according to established inclusion and exclusion criteria, and analyzed using Bibliometrix (R-package) and VOSviewer.The study will evaluate annual publication trends, citation performance, influential authors, institutions, countries, journals, collaborative networks, keyword co-occurrence, thematic evolution, and emerging research hotspots.The findings are expected to provide a comprehensive overview of the intellectual structure and development of AI-driven drug delivery research, identify influential contributors and collaborative patterns, and highlight promising directions for future investigations.The study also seeks to offer practical insights for researchers, pharmaceutical scientists, healthcare professionals, policymakers, and industry stakeholders by identifying technological innovations that can enhance drug development processes and improve patient-centric therapeutic outcomes.By integrating bibliometric techniques with science mapping, this study contributes to the growing body of knowledge on AI-enabled pharmaceutical technologies and provides a strategic research agenda for advancing intelligent drug delivery systems.

candidates.title: RiboGRAM learns multi-scale non-coding RNA grammar for structural and regulatory inference
candidates.abstract: Protein-coding sequences are read through the triplet genetic code, whereas the organization of molecular information within non-coding RNA sequences remains elusive. Here, we identify a non-coding RNA grammar defined by multi-scale motif usage and 5'-to-3' positional gradients, and develop RiboGRAM to learn this organization. Across nine organisms, non-coding RNAs showed scale-dependent divergence from coding sequences, with directional U-rich and AU-rich gradients. Integrating multi-scale sequence encoding with contextual modeling, RiboGRAM organized RNA families, revealing motif-associated and pair-like patterns across layers. Without structural supervision, non-coding RNA pretraining improved base-pair recovery over coding or messenger RNA pretraining, with representations supporting alignment-free diffusion-based 3D modeling of short RNAs. In human RNA-protein binding profiles, RiboGRAM identified position-resolved motif organization across protein targets and cell types, with sequence-preference shifts associated with reduced cross-cell transferability. Together, these results establish a learnable grammar of non-coding RNA sequence organization for structural and regulatory inference.

candidates.title: Tensorizing Pairwise Structural Analysis: GPU-Accelerated RMSD and FCC Clustering in HADDOCK3 Without Structural Regression.
candidates.abstract: Integrative macromolecular docking pipelines generate thousands of candidate structural decoys, relying on downstream pairwise ensemble analysis, including Root-Mean-Square Deviation (RMSD) matrices and Fraction of Common Contacts (FCC) clustering, to identify biologically relevant binding poses. However, pairwise structural comparisons scale quadratically (O(N^2)), and canonical workflows in HADDOCK3 historically rely on disk-bound trajectory serialization and iterative CPU set operations, creating a quadratic computational and storage bottleneck for large ensembles. Here, we demonstrate that these operations can be reformulated as continuous linear algebra on GPU-resident tensors: structural superposition via batched Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) and residue contact overlap via binary matrix multiplication (M = A A^T). Across empirical benchmarks spanning N = 200 to 10,000 models (evaluating up to 49,995,000 decoy pairs), our GPU implementation achieves a 6.41-fold compute speedup on Apple Silicon (MPS) and up to 12.2-fold end-to-end acceleration in an N = 5,000 ablation on NVIDIA CUDA by eliminating trajectory disk I/O. Crucially, the implementation achieves zero downstream structural regression relative to canonical baselines, preserving identical cluster assignments (Adjusted Rand Index ARI = 1.0000, zero differing assignments) with sub-microangstrom RMSD concordance (Delta_max <= 4.07 x 10^-7 Angstrom on single-precision MPS; machine-precision Delta_max <= 8.88 x 10^-16 Angstrom on double-precision CUDA). The accelerated code, test suites, and benchmarking workflows are openly accessible on GitHub under the Apache-2.0 license.

candidates.title: The specific interface for selenocysteine-decoding tRNA in HIV-1 Gag MAdomain regulates progeny virion infectivity
candidates.abstract: Localization of HIV-1 particle assembly at the plasma membrane (PM) is mediated by the HIV-1 Gag matrix (MA) domain. Competing binding of PM acidic phospholipids and cellular tRNAs to MA-highly basic region (MA-HBR) likely regulate the PM-specific binding of Gag; however, the specificity of the MA-tRNA interaction and its role in viral replication remain poorly understood. Here, using a modified crosslinking-immunoprecipitation (CLIP)-sequencing workflow for identifying MA-bound tRNAs, we determined that most MA-bound tRNAs were also abundantly present in cells. However, selenocysteine-tRNA (SeCTCA) is overrepresented among Gag-bound tRNAs despite its paucity. The binding of SeCTCA to Gag is entirely dependent on MA-HBR, whereas non-SeCTCA tRNAs can bind Gag through both MA and nucleocapsid domains. Structure prediction of MA-tRNA complexes revealed the binding interface unique to the MA-SeCTCA complex, which was verified experimentally. CLIP experiments demonstrated that this interface is specifically needed for the MA binding to SeCTCA but not to other tRNAs. Notably, disruption of this interface altered Gag localization pattern, reduced infectivity of virions, and impaired virus replication in CD4+ T cells. Collectively, our results indicate that SeCTCA tRNA binds the HIV-1 Gag MA domain with high specificity and promotes virion formation and efficient replication in T cells.

candidates.title: XAI-driven analysis of influencing factors in streamflow-based flood forecasting via fine tuned MTV19Anet
candidates.abstract: An accurate and timely flood prediction that relies on streamflow information is important for developing an early warning system to minimize the negative effects of floods. This paper proposes a new Steam flow-based Flood prediction model using a Fine-tuned MTV19ANet architecture (SFFPM-FTA). The novelty of proposed model integrates an Enhanced Normalization Technique (enNormT) that effectively reduces the impact of large outliers. It also employs an improved entropy-based feature extraction method to enhance prediction robustness. The hyperparameters are optimized using an Improved Wolverine Optimization Algorithm (IWoOA) with SHAP, an explainable AI technique to insights into model interpretability. The study also includes the visual representation of steam flow, where normal flow and flooded flow are visually represented over river areas. The experimental analysis shows that the proposed SFFPM-FTA model obtains high performance compared to other prediction models with respect to various error measures. The proposed model demonstrates minimal errors in streamflow-based flood forecasting through improved normalization during preprocessing and enhanced entropy-based feature extraction. Compared with other baseline methods, the proposed method demonstrates superior performance, with reductions of 55.26% in MAE, 64.56% in MAPE, 83.45% in MSE, and 57.30% in RMSE, respectively. In addition, the model achieves NSE of 0.988, KGE of 0.963, and R² of 0.986, demonstrating its effectiveness in accurately capturing streamflow dynamics. Overall, the proposed SFFPM-FTA improves flood forecasting accuracy and provides reliable and interpretable streamflow predictions.

candidates.title: Pectinase-Based Bioprocesses for Circular Bioeconomy and Sustainable Industrial Development.
candidates.abstract: Pectinases play a vital role in the degradation of pectic part of the plant cell wall and are considered in the group of hydrolytic enzymes. In the present scenario, demand of economically feasible and environment friendly techniques and approaches has significantly led the research on the microbial production, standardization of process parameters and improvements of pectinases. The development of pectinase-based bioprocesses has been found to promote sustainable industrial practices by reducing the use of chemicals, energy, and waste, thereby supporting eco-friendly production systems. The unique aspect of this review is that it explains traditional methods of pectinase production alongside novel methods, which include solid-state and submerged fermentation, recombinant DNA techniques, heterologous gene expression, protein engineering, CRISPR/Cas genome editing technologies, enzyme immobilization, and nanobiotechnological methods, which improve the production, stability, and performance of pectinases. It further demonstrates the increasing importance of the use of pectinases in sustainable manufacturing through decreasing the use of chemicals and energy, as well as reducing waste production from industry. It illustrates that innovations in microbial strain engineering, process optimization, and utilization of low-cost substrates have significantly increased the economic viability and efficiency of producing pectinases. Yet, some issues associated with commercialization, standardization of production processes, recovery, and stability of enzymes still exist. Overall, this review paper gives an overview of the recent advancements and limitations of next-generation pectinases.

candidates.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
candidates.abstract: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-performance validation.
